accepted.s: According to Census 2011, what was the literacy rate of Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: The Census 2011 literacy rate of Andhra Pradesh was 67.35%. India’s corresponding literacy rate was 72.98%.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact official figure from a closely similar reported value.
accepted.sec: Education outcome indicators - literacy, GER, dropout, PGI, ASER

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the literacy figures cited for Andhra Pradesh?
o: Census 2011 recorded 67.41%, while some compilations cite 67.35%.
Census 2011 recorded 83%, while some compilations cite 73%.
Census 2011 recorded 72.98%, while some compilations cite 67.35%.
Census 2011 recorded 67.35%, while some compilations cite 67.41%.
accepted.x: The Census 2011 figure given for Andhra Pradesh is 67.35%; some compilations cite 67.41%. The figures of 73% and 83% relate to the Minister’s statement on Akshara Andhra, not the Census 2011 figure.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two closely resembling percentages associated with the same indicator.
accepted.sec: Education outcome indicators - literacy, GER, dropout, PGI, ASER

accepted.s: The Minister stated that the Akshara Andhra initiative had raised literacy from approximately which level to which level?
accepted.x: The Minister stated that Akshara Andhra had raised literacy from 73% to 83%.
accepted.tq: Use the paired before-and-after figures rather than the Census literacy figures.
accepted.sec: Education outcome indicators - literacy, GER, dropout, PGI, ASER

accepted.s: A door-to-door survey conducted in Andhra Pradesh from 12 June to 12 July 2025 identified how many out-of-school children, all of whom were reportedly mainstreamed?
accepted.x: The survey identified 1,60,196 out-of-school children, and all of them were mainstreamed.
accepted.tq: Read the Indian-style digit grouping carefully when identifying the exact survey figure.
accepted.sec: Education outcome indicators - literacy, GER, dropout, PGI, ASER

accepted.s: Which statement best reflects the contrasting figures associated with school dropouts in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The survey found 1,60,196 out-of-school children, while the Minister cited nearly one lakh dropouts.
The survey found nearly one lakh out-of-school children, while the Minister cited 1,60,196 dropouts.
The survey found no out-of-school children, while the Minister cited 1,60,196 dropouts.
Both the survey and the Minister cited exactly 1,60,196 dropouts.
accepted.x: The door-to-door survey found 1,60,196 out-of-school children, whereas the Minister separately cited nearly one lakh dropouts.
accepted.tq: Separate two similar but non-identical figures reported in different contexts.
accepted.sec: Education outcome indicators - literacy, GER, dropout, PGI, ASER

accepted.s: The Andhra Model of Education aims at achieving:
accepted.x: The Andhra Model of Education aims at 100% enrolment.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise stated objective instead of substituting a related education goal.
accepted.sec: Education outcome indicators - literacy, GER, dropout, PGI, ASER

accepted.s:
With reference to Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL) in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. Language skills rose from 21% to 47%.
2. Mathematics skills rose from 20% to 50%.
3. Language skills rose from 20% to 50%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 reverses the language and mathematics figures.
accepted.tq: Match each intervention outcome with its correct subject-wise before-and-after figures.
accepted.sec: Education outcome indicators - literacy, GER, dropout, PGI, ASER

accepted.s: The LEAP initiative in Andhra Pradesh primarily responds to:
o: Poor learning outcomes reported by ASER
The shortage of higher education institutions reported by the Census
The shortage of trained health workers under the Universal Health Policy
The decline in health expenditure reported by the SDG Index
accepted.x: LEAP responds to poor learning outcomes reported by ASER.
accepted.tq: Link the initiative to the problem it is designed to address.
accepted.sec: Education outcome indicators - literacy, GER, dropout, PGI, ASER

accepted.s: What was the total expenditure provided in the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026–27?
accepted.x: The total expenditure in the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026–27 was ₹3,32,205 crore.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the total budget size from the education-sector allocation.
accepted.sec: Social sector expenditure share in AP Budget

accepted.s: Which department received the largest allocation in the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026–27, and what was the allocation?
accepted.x: The School Education Department received ₹32,308 crore and was the largest department in the Budget 2026–27.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure department–allocation pair and reject swapped department names.
accepted.sec: Social sector expenditure share in AP Budget

accepted.s: The allocation for Higher Education in the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026–27 was:
accepted.x: Higher Education received an allocation of ₹2,567 crore in the Budget 2026–27.
accepted.tq: Separate the higher education allocation from the much larger school education allocation.
accepted.sec: Social sector expenditure share in AP Budget

accepted.s: The sector-wise total allocation for Health and Family Welfare in the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026–27 was:
accepted.x: The sector-wise total for Health and Family Welfare was ₹19,630 crore. This differs from the ₹19,306 crore allocation mentioned for the Health Department.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a department allocation from the broader sector-wise total.
accepted.sec: Social sector expenditure share in AP Budget

accepted.s:
With reference to the education sector in the Andhra Pradesh Budget, consider the following statements:
1. The education sector as a whole received ₹35,673 crore.
2. It accounted for 11.7% of total spending.
3. The average share for all States was 14.5%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The education sector received ₹35,673 crore, constituting 11.7% of spending, compared with the 14.5% average for all States.
accepted.tq: Compare the State’s sectoral share with the benchmark average while retaining the allocation figure.
accepted.sec: Social sector expenditure share in AP Budget

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the expenditure shares mentioned for welfare and debt service in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Welfare 17 paise and debt service 18 paise per rupee
Welfare 18 paise and debt service 17 paise per rupee
Both welfare and debt service 17 paise per rupee
Both welfare and debt service 18 paise per rupee
accepted.x: Welfare accounted for 17 paise of every rupee, while debt service accounted for 18 paise. They were described as being broadly at the same level.
accepted.tq: Keep adjacent expenditure-share figures in their correct order.
accepted.sec: Social sector expenditure share in AP Budget

accepted.s: In the 2024–25 Budget Estimates, the ten main social and economic heads together accounted for what share of total spending?
accepted.x: The ten main social and economic heads together accounted for 68% of spending in the 2024–25 Budget Estimates.
accepted.tq: Identify the aggregate share rather than confusing it with individual department percentages.
accepted.sec: Social sector expenditure share in AP Budget

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh secured which score and band in the SDG India Index 2023–24?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh scored 74 and was placed in the Front Runner band in the SDG India Index 2023–24.
accepted.tq: Pair the numerical score with its correct performance band.
accepted.sec: SDG India Index - AP scores on health and education

accepted.s: The rollout of the Sanjeevani initiative in Andhra Pradesh was associated with which month and year?
accepted.x: The Sanjeevani rollout was associated with August 2026.
accepted.tq: Use the chronology of current initiatives to identify the correct rollout period.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Universal Health Policy referred to for Andhra Pradesh provides coverage of:
accepted.x: The Universal Health Policy provides coverage of ₹2.5 lakh.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the policy coverage amount from nearby rounded figures.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The health outlay in Andhra Pradesh was reported to have increased by:
accepted.x: The health outlay was reported to have increased by 9.5%.
accepted.tq: Separate a year-on-year outlay increase from budget share percentages.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the controversy relating to Vaidya Seva in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Hospitals halted services over unpaid dues of ₹300 crore, and the opposition supported the insurance model.
Hospitals halted services over unpaid dues of ₹3,000 crore, and the opposition called the insurance model a dilution of Aarogyasri.
Hospitals halted services over unpaid dues of ₹30,000 crore, and the opposition called for replacing Aarogyasri with Vaidya Seva.
Hospitals halted services over unpaid dues of ₹3,000 crore, and the opposition described the model as strengthening Aarogyasri.
accepted.x: Hospitals halted services over ₹3,000 crore of unpaid Vaidya Seva dues. The opposition criticised the insurance model as a dilution of Aarogyasri.
accepted.tq: Check both the amount of unpaid dues and the direction of the political criticism.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh’s demographic and health indicators is correct?
o: The TFR of Andhra Pradesh is 2.5, which is above replacement level.
Only the IMR of Andhra Pradesh is better than the national goal.
The TFR of Andhra Pradesh is 1.5, which is well below replacement level.
The MMR, IMR and TFR of Andhra Pradesh are all worse than the national goals.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh’s MMR, IMR and TFR are all better than the national goals. Its TFR is 1.5, well below replacement level.
accepted.tq: Reject the reversed comparison and focus on the exact fertility figure.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
